annotator_prompt.name: lifted_count
annotator_prompt.description: When several highlighted cubes had to be picked up, the prescribed red-first, increasing-world-y order contradicted the recorded pickups. A highlighted blue cube was lifted and returned before green and red were handled, and among two highlighted blue cubes the larger-world-y cube was handled first. Consequently the prefix count could remain zero after a real completed pickup, making later target selection fail SUFFICIENCY. Replace the fixed order with blue, green, red, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use decreasing original world y, then increasing original world x for ties. Establish identities and this order from highlight_frame, never from positions changed by handling. Keep the field as the number of completed lifts in this fixed prefix. Initialize to 0 and increment only at the cycle observing the next target held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15. Do not increment at grasp or when commanding the lift, and do not decrement after returning a cube. For example, after the first highlighted blue cube has visibly reached lift height, write 1 and preserve 1 through its release and retreat. Reannotate subsequent counts using this corrected order; no additional memory field is needed.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: lifted_count
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: With a highlighted blue cube already lifted and returned, the old red-first order left the completed-prefix count at zero and made the policy select red instead of the next green target. The same conflict occurred between two highlighted blue cubes ordered by increasing world y. This breaks SUFFICIENCY and would break PREDICTABILITY if the annotation were corrected without changing the policy's definition. Replace the order with blue, green, red, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use decreasing original world y, then increasing original world x for ties. Recover identities and their original order from highlight_frame. Initialize lifted_count to 0. Using the carried count, identify the next uncounted target; increment by one only when this cycle's motion frames and current state show that target newly lifted and held off the table at TCP approximately z=0.15. For example, write 1 after the first blue target's completed lift and retain it through release and retreat. Do not increment for a low grasp, a commanded lift, an empty grasp, a previously counted cube still held, or an action executing no steps. Preserve all other existing completion checks.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
After the button operation, the old target-order rule selected red instead of the recorded blue target, or the smaller-world-y blue cube instead of the larger-world-y one. After a completed lift and return, the inconsistent count again selected the wrong target. These are SUFFICIENCY failures, not reasons for cycle-specific exceptions. Replace every red-green-blue and increasing-world-y ordering clause with the same fixed order used by memory: blue, green, red, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use decreasing original world y, then increasing original world x for ties. Match individual highlighted identities from highlight_frame and do not reorder after handling. Recognize a newly completed lift from this cycle's observations before choosing the next action. Retain the existing return-and-retreat rules: a counted cube still held is returned only if another target remains, a low open hand retracts before lateral travel, and an open hand already hovering over the selected uncounted cube descends and closes rather than switching targets or repeating the hover. Remove the conflicting old ordering clauses entirely.

A separate open-hand approach to the correct highlighted cube was displaced by more than 1 cm and used a reflected yaw despite available calibration. This is a geometry-to-waypoint SUFFICIENCY failure, not missing historical information. Make the existing calibrated localization rule operational: for image pixel p=(u,v,1), form the world ray origin C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1 p. Intersect the ray with the relevant surface plane z=h using X=C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. For resting cubes use the top-face height inferred from cube geometry, not the tabletop plane or the projected center of the entire visible silhouette. Localize the top-face center, refine with the current wrist view, and use its world x,y with the prescribed TCP approach height z=0.15. Reconstruct two endpoints of a top-face edge on that same plane, compute theta=atan2(delta_y,delta_x), and choose among theta+k*pi/2 the edge-aligned yaw nearest the current hand yaw. Do not negate theta based on image appearance or copy an image-plane edge angle. Keep that alignment for descent and lift. Retain the existing approximately 1–1.5 cm hover tolerance and object-centered descent rule.
proposal.refused: Some reports described the first handled target as a red cube and proposed remembering whether red had already been lifted. The full trajectories show that the first handled cube was blue, followed by green and then red. The report calling the blue cube beneath the hand a highlighted rear red cube is therefore not passed on, nor is a red-specific completion field or selection exception. The corrected common ordering and existing lifted_count represent the actual history. Likewise, the proposal to choose green despite an unchanged zero count is not retained as an action exception: the count must become 1 when the preceding blue lift is observed. Requests to descend when already within hover tolerance and to preserve highlighted identities despite occlusion are already covered by the action instructions; they require consistent target selection, not additional memory or separate special-case rules.

fields.name: highlight_frame
fields.description: Write null when memory is empty and no cube highlight has appeared. If the carried value is null, inspect all motion frames and store the earliest frame clearly showing white circular areas beneath the highlighted cubes. Ignore the white square beneath the button. Once a label is stored, carry it unchanged even when the white areas disappear. e.g. "E17"
fields.annotation: Initially null. On the first cycle containing visible white circular areas beneath cubes, store the earliest frame in that cycle clearly showing the highlighted set. Retain that label thereafter, including after the highlights disappear. The white square supporting the button is not a cube highlight. e.g. "E17"

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Initialize false. Set true when this cycle shows the closed fingertips down in contact with the button following a pressing descent, including a contact-limited TCP height around z=0.024. Otherwise preserve the carried value. Highlights alone do not establish a press. e.g. false
fields.annotation: Initially false. Set true at the first cycle showing the closed fingertips down in contact with the button after the pressing descent; the observed TCP may stop around z=0.024 rather than reaching the commanded z=0.0075. Keep true thereafter. Do not set true merely because highlights appear. e.g. false

fields.name: lifted_count
fields.description: Initialize zero. Recover the highlighted identities and their fixed order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, omitting unhighlighted colors; within each color use increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties. Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. The carried count excludes the completed prefix of this fixed order. Increment the carried count by one only when this cycle shows the next not-yet-counted target held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15 after lifting. Use the current motion frames and held-cube identity to distinguish a newly completed lift from a previously counted target still being held. Do not increment for a low grasp, a commanded lift, an empty grasp, or an action executing no steps. A previously counted target must not increment it again. Preserve the count through release and retreat. e.g. 0
fields.annotation: Initially zero. Count distinct highlighted cubes whose completed pickup lift has been observed: the cube is held off the table and the TCP has reached approximately z=0.15. Increment at the cycle observing that lift, not at the grasp or at the cycle commanding the lift. Returning a cube to the table does not decrement the count. Establish a fixed target order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue color order, omitting unhighlighted colors; within a color use increasing world y, then increasing world x for ties. Do not reorder using positions changed by handling. The count is the length of the completed prefix of this order; increment only for the next target's completed lift, never again for a previously counted target. e.g. 0

texts.action:
Start with an open hand and approach the button. Interpret all positions in world coordinates using the supplied camera calibration; estimate button and cube locations from their geometry, not raw image left/right. Back-project a visible surface center onto that surface's horizontal height plane, not automatically onto z=0. Estimate surface height and center from object geometry and both calibrated current views where available. For pixel p=(u,v,1), use the corresponding camera's calibration to compute world ray origin C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1 p. Intersect with the surface plane z=h using X=C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Use the current wrist camera's extrinsics for wrist pixels, not the front camera's extrinsics. For the button, localize the raised circular pressing surface rather than its white base. For a resting cube, localize the top-face center at the cube's top height inferred from its geometry, not the tabletop plane or the center of the entire visible silhouette. Refine this estimate with the current calibrated wrist view. Use the resulting world x,y for object-centered approach and contact waypoints, retaining the separately specified TCP waypoint heights. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. Approximate hover alignment permits the next operation but does not make the achieved TCP x,y the object center. Recover target identities from highlight_frame after their white areas disappear, matching by position as well as color; never select every cube of a highlighted color. Use the observations of this cycle together with carried memory to recognize newly completed presses and lifts before selecting the action.

Button rules: If button_pressed is false and the hand is not yet above the button, move to its center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. At approximate button hover, allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm to proceed to the next operation, but do not treat the achieved TCP x,y as the button center. Before closing and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, refining it with the wrist image. With open fingers at approximate hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact yet, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075 with fingers closed. Once contact is observed, retract to the button center at z=0.15, keeping closed; do not repeat the press merely because the actual contact height is higher than the command. After retracting, open at the button approach waypoint before traveling to a cube.

Pickup rules: Establish the fixed target order from highlight_frame: red, green, blue, then increasing world y within each color, with increasing world x for ties. Robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Match individual identities by position as well as color; do not reorder using positions changed by handling. Interpret lifted_count as excluding the completed prefix, including any newly completed lift observed this cycle. Select the next uncounted identity before testing whether the hand is aligned for descent. With open fingers and adequate table clearance, approach its center at z=0.15. Use roll=3.1416 and pitch=0. Back-project two endpoints of a cube top-face edge onto the same top-face height plane using the calibrated ray-plane intersection. From their world-coordinate difference compute theta=atan2(delta_y,delta_x). Choose among theta+k*pi/2, for integer k, the square-equivalent edge-aligned yaw requiring the least angular rotation from the current hand yaw, accounting for angle wrapping. Do not negate theta based on image appearance or copy an image-plane edge angle. Preserve that alignment during descent and lift. Only when the open hand is approximately aligned above the selected uncounted target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm; if already aligned, descend rather than commanding another hover. An open hand at hover above a returned, counted cube must instead approach the next uncounted target at z=0.15 with fingers open. With the cube grasped at low height, lift vertically to z=0.15 with fingers closed, preserving the aligned yaw. Estimate its grasp center from the visible cube and wrist geometry rather than treating a small TCP tracking error as a new target location.

Handling additional targets: Once a pickup lift is visibly complete, it counts even if the cube is subsequently returned. If another highlighted target remains and a counted cube is still held at hover height, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.01, retaining current orientation, and open on arrival. If the hand is low and open over that returned cube, retract vertically to approximately z=0.15 with fingers open before moving laterally. When retracted, approach the next uncounted target, not the cube just returned. After lifting the final target, keep it held; success should end the episode without requiring a placement.

For every gripper-only change, first construct the nominal object-centered waypoint rather than copying the achieved TCP pose. If that waypoint already provides at least 2 mm of translation from the reported TCP pose, do not add a nudge. Otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm so that the translation is at least 2 mm. Do not advance memory on an action that executed no steps. If alignment or grasp evidence is ambiguous, use the current wrist image to correct the relevant object-centered approach at safe height; a failed empty grasp should be retried without counting it. If no target evidence has yet been captured after the button operation, use a short bounded wait specifically to observe the highlight display and inspect every returned frame. Do not invent targets or repeatedly press a confirmed button. For an otherwise unmatched situation, preserve known task facts, keep a visibly held cube closed, and retract vertically to safe clearance before reassessing.
